marks.gloss_en: ואי מכללא מאי? דאי מכללא, לעולם אהבה רבה הוו אמרי, וכי מטא זמן יוצר אור הוו אמרי ליה, ומאי ברכות אין מעכבות זו את זו -- סדר ברכות: if inferred, the inference does not go through -- they may have said אהבה רבה and יוצר אור when its time came, and 'not impeding' means the ORDER of the blessings does not impede (= p_seder_berachot); the deflection is not refuted
the possible reading offered at 12a.3: 'the blessings do not impede one another' means their ORDER does not impede -- not that one may be said without the other
תניא נמי הכי, רבי נתן אומר: בגבולין בקשו לקרות כן -- R' Natan's baraita says the same: the outlying areas sought to read the Ten Commandments
תניא נמי הכי, רבי נתן אומר: ...אלא שכבר בטלום מפני תרעומת המינין -- and that they were abolished because of the heretics' grievance
אמר ליה רב חסדא: כבר בטלום מפני תרעומת המינין -- they have already been abolished because of the heretics' grievance; nothing is answered
Rabba bar bar Chana thought to institute [the reading of the Ten Commandments] in Sura
אמר ליה רב אשי: כבר בטלום מפני תרעומת המינין -- the same reply to Ameimar; nothing is answered
Ameimar thought to institute [the reading of the Ten Commandments] in Nehardea
the mishnah (Tamid 5:1): [the priests in the Temple] read the Ten Commandments, Shema, VeHaya im Shamoa, VaYomer, Emet veYatziv, Avoda and the priestly blessing
even in the outlying areas they sought to read thus [the Ten Commandments with the Shema]
the mishnah (Tamid 5:1): on Shabbat they add one blessing for the outgoing priestly watch
שנאמר להגיד בבקר חסדך -- 'in the morning' pairs the morning with kindness; hence emet veyatziv in the morning
ואמונתך בלילות -- 'in the nights' pairs the night with faith; hence emet ve'emuna in the evening
whoever did not say emet veyatziv in the morning has not discharged his obligation
תא שמע: שחרית פתח במעריב ערבים וסיים ביוצר אור -- יצא (and its evening mirror); כללו של דבר הכל הולך אחר החתום -- so in the beer/wine case too the conclusion decides
in the morning, one who opened with 'who forms light' and concluded with 'who brings on evenings' has not fulfilled his obligation

שאני התם דקאמר ברוך יוצר המאורות -- there the conclusion is itself a complete blessing, so following it proves nothing for a short blessing over beer. CHALLENGED (12a.17): הניחא לרב, who said any blessing without the Name is no blessing -- fine; but for R' Yochanan, who said any blessing without kingship is no blessing, the conclusion יוצר המאורות has no kingship, so what is there to say? DEFENDED (12a.18): אלא, since Rabba bar Ulla said the wording is so as to mention the attribute of day at night and of night by day, the blessing-and-kingship said at the opening is said for both, so the conclusion counts as a full blessing on R' Yochanan's view too. The deflection stands; the schema cannot say that a deflection was defended, so the exchange lives here
תא שמע מסיפא: כללו של דבר הכל הולך אחר החתום -- what does 'the general principle' come to include? לאו לאתויי הא דאמרן -- is it not the case we stated?

לא, לאתויי נהמא ותמרי -- no: it comes to include bread and dates. Which case? not ate-bread-thought-dates (that is our question: the hypothesis h_leatuyei_nahama, rejected), but ate-dates-thought-bread, opened with bread in mind and concluded with dates -- fulfilled, since even the bread formula would have sufficed over dates, which nourish (12a.21-22). So the klal teaches nothing about our case
entertained: the principle comes to include one who ate bread, thought he ate dates, opened with dates in mind and concluded with the bread formula
דאפילו סיים בדנהמא נמי יצא -- since even concluding with the bread formula over dates fulfils, concluding with the dates formula certainly does
the principle is needed for one who ate dates, thought he ate bread, opened with the bread formula in mind and concluded with the dates formula
מאי טעמא -- דתמרי נמי מיזן זייני: dates too nourish, so the bread formula covers them after the fact
the reason: dates too nourish [so the bread formula, which speaks of nourishment, covers them after the fact]
the candidate resolution: holding beer he thought wine, opened with wine in mind and concluded with the beer formula -- if everything follows the conclusion, he has fulfilled his obligation
in the evening, one who opened with 'who brings on evenings' and concluded with 'who forms light' has not fulfilled his obligation
the baraita's general principle: everything follows the conclusion [of the blessing]
Rav: any blessing that has no mention of the Name is not a blessing
Rabba bar Ulla: [the wording of the light and evening blessings is] so as to mention the attribute of day at night and the attribute of night by day
דאי נמי אם אמר שהכל נהיה בדברו יצא -- since even the blessing he set out to say would have sufficed, the wine formula he actually concluded with certainly does
דהא תנן: על כולם אם אמר שהכל נהיה בדברו יצא -- a mishnah citation (no support kind names a דתנן; svara stands in): שהכל over wine is valid after the fact
the mishnah (11a): where the Sages said to lengthen [a blessing, one may not shorten it]
מאי טעמא דרב -- דכתיב ה' זוקף כפופים: the Lord is the one who raises the bowed
'the Lord raises the bowed' (Ps 146:8)
מתיבי: מפני שמי נחת הוא -- the verse has one lowered in connection with the Name, against straightening at it
'he was lowered before My name' (Mal 2:5)
מי כתיב בשמי? מפני שמי כתיב -- the lowering is 'before' the Name, not 'at' it (= p_mipnei_lo_bishmi)
the verse does not say 'at My name' but 'before My name' -- the lowering is before the Name, not at it
one who prays, when he bows, bows at 'Blessed'
